episode_summary: Episode 392 (May 2022): a roundtable of the hosts on soulbound tokens and NFT badges, whether crypto is an iteration of existing systems or an expansion of money, USDC and Circle versus Tether, tokenizing intangible value, and the economics and risks of crypto.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host defined a soulbound token as a token issued to a wallet that can never move from that private key.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: a soul bound token is a token that is issued to your wallet, that private key, and it cannot move from that private key.

cards.claim: In May 2022 the hosts described soulbound tokens as non-transferable NFTs, also called NTTs.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's an nft the type of like a non-trans non-fungible token that is also not transferable

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host likened unwanted non-transferable tokens that cannot be removed to a digital STD.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's a digital STD, bro.

cards.claim: In May 2022 the hosts said Algorand, unlike Ethereum, does not let tokens be airdropped without the account's permission.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: that you actually can't airdrop. You can't essentially send tokens to an account without getting that account's permission.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host explained that NFT-based voting could be gamed if voters could transfer their token after casting a vote.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if I'm not really, really careful about things, then someone could vote and then transfer the NFT.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host suggested NFTs could work well as time-limited software licenses that are bought and resold.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Like software licenses could be really good for this.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host explained POAPs as proof-of-attendance tokens that show someone was at an event and can be used to reach those attendees.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: But it stands for proof of attendance protocol, where you basically have an indicator

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued the word wallet was a silly name for crypto software that does not actually hold coins.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: that is a silly silly word for how you're actually using this thing

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued that credential-style soulbound badges, such as a class-completion NFT, should not be sellable.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: You cannot pass those things around. You can't sell that.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host said Unlock Protocol already issues time-based membership tokens that expire and must be renewed.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: unlock protocol does that yeah they have time-based tokens

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued ERC-20 and NFT adoption took off because shared standards let exchanges and wallets interoperate.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the only reason why erc20s blew up and nfcs blew up is because the standard exists around them

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host agreed much of Web3 was recreating Web2 ideas and said rebuilding them on a new environment is not a bad thing.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: a lot of it is just recreating the wheel

cards.claim: The hosts recalled that during a 10-words-or-less blockchain question in an interview with Boosie, his PR person whispered to say decentralized and privacy.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: his pr guy leans over and whispers in his ears like say decentralized say privacy say

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued USDC was lobbying to become the digital legal tender of the United States.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think it's very obvious at this point that USDC is like lobbying to try and be the digital legal tender for the United States.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued confidence in USDC was higher than in USDT because its reserves were easier to audit.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I would argue that it's easier to have higher confidence

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host claimed Circle had been the largest Bitcoin exchange on the planet for years, a claim the hosts offered a $50 bounty to fact-check.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: was the largest Bitcoin exchange on the planet for many, many, many, many years

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host said Circle bought Poloniex because it was then the largest Ether exchange in the hemisphere.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they bought poloniex because poloniex was the largest ether exchange in in this hemisphere

cards.claim: In May 2022 the hosts said a one million dollar bounty was offered for a reasonable audit of Tether's reserves.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's a there's a one million dollar bounty out on anyone who can provide a reasonable audit of tether's uh reserves

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host predicted USDC would become the legal tender stamp of the United States.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: is going to be that legal tender stamp

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued USDC was us money while Bitcoin and Ethereum were them money.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: There is us, and there is them. USDC is us money.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host said soulbound tokens were a terrible name and that crypto needed catchier names for mass adoption.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: soulbound tokens are a terrible name for anything

cards.claim: In May 2022 the hosts debated whether crypto is just an iteration of existing systems, with one host arguing it is an expansion of what money is.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: crypto is just an iteration

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued that blockchains and web3 are an expansion of what money is, not merely an iteration.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's an expansion of what money is in my opinion

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host cited Disney's $67.4 billion market cap and estimated its intangible assets at $10 to $20 billion.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: They have a certain market cap for Disney. $67.4 billion.

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host predicted crypto would let people capture intangible value, such as Disney's roughly $20 billion in intangibles, as tokens.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: you're going to be able to capture that 20 billion in tokens that's what crypto will do

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host said crypto's fast-moving, lightly regulated markets were a cesspool where people get taken advantage of.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: that's just like a cesspool for like being taken advantage of

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host cited PulseChain as an example of a project heavily marketed without much underlying value.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: you have things like you know pulse chain like people building something marketing the shit out of it and it not reasonably being anything worth of value

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host argued the point of crypto was not to let people invest in things for profit.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the point of all this stuff isn't so that we can allow people to invest in things

cards.claim: In May 2022 a host said a certificate of deposit paid roughly 0.03% interest.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: CDs will give you 0.03% back.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #392-It is Bubble Season , What Are You Carrying ?
